meta.title: Procode
meta.description: From zero to pro in Claude Code: what you'll spend for the way you work, which model fits, and what to learn first.

mascot.name: Tilde
mascot.greet: Meow! I'm Tilde. I'll help you go from zero to pro in Claude Code.
mascot.greet2: Answer seven questions and I'll map your trail: what to learn, which model and skills fit you, and what you'll spend.
mascot.askName: First, what should I call you?
mascot.askUse: Great, {name}. What will you mostly use Claude Code for?
mascot.askExp: How much have you used it so far?
mascot.askTime: How much time will you spend with it?
mascot.askModel: Which model will you work with? If you're not sure, Sonnet is the starting point the docs recommend.
mascot.askFeatures: Last one: what do you want to add? Green ones save tokens; the rest add power and usage.
mascot.done: All set, {name}! Your trail is below: start with the first step. Your estimated usage is in the Usage section.
mascot.reactCheap: That fits comfortably in the Pro plan.
mascot.reactMid: That pace calls for a Max plan.
mascot.reactHigh: Whoa, heavy usage! Check the tips to save.
mascot.askRole: And what do you do? That way I can recommend the skills and plugins that fit you.

onboarding.effortHint: More effort means more reasoning tokens, billed as output. Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 default to medium.

learn.d: Understand unfamiliar code, learn a language, ask questions.

fixes.d: Fix errors, tweak styles, one-off tasks.

fullstack.d: Full features in an app, every day.

refactor.d: Migrations, changes across many files, audits.

automation.d: CI, PR reviews, scheduled tasks, scripts.

some.d: I can ask for basic things.

daily.d: I want to get everything out of it.

haiku.d: The fastest and cheapest. Great for exploration and subagents.

opus.d: Complex reasoning and architecture. The default model on Pro and Max.

fable.d: The most capable, for the longest and hardest tasks. The most expensive.

clear.d: Start fresh when you switch topics. Stale context is paid for on every message.

plan.d: Claude explores and proposes before touching code. Avoids redoing work.

hooks.d: Scripts that trim long output (tests, logs) before Claude reads it.

codeintel.d: Language plugin: jumps to definitions instead of reading whole files.

skills.d: Reusable instructions and workflows that load only when needed.

mcp.d: Connect Claude to GitHub, Notion, databases, the browser…

subagents.d: Workers with their own context that hand you back a summary.

advisor.d: A stronger model Claude consults at key moments.

loop.d: Repeat a prompt every X minutes while the session is open.

ultracode.d: Claude orchestrates many subagents from a script for big jobs.

teams.d: Several coordinated Claude instances. Experimental and very expensive.

fast.d: Faster Opus at twice the price. Only affects Opus.

results.title: Your estimated usage
results.lead: What you'd spend on the API with this usage. On Pro and Max you don't pay per token: usage counts against your plan's limits.
results.planNote: Our heuristic: Anthropic doesn't publish a dollar equivalent for each plan. Max 5x and Max 20x give 5 and 20 times Pro's per-session usage, with limits that reset every 5 hours and every week. /usage shows how much you have left.
results.disclaimer: Estimate. Real usage depends on project size, session length and how much Claude reads. Calibrated against the official average: about US$13 per developer per active day, and under US$30 for 90% of users.

pro.d: Enough for learning and light to moderate use.

max5.d: For working with Claude Code several hours a day.

max20.d: Heavy all-day use, with Opus and subagents.

max20plus.d: At this volume you'll likely exceed the limits. Turn on usage credits or pay through the API with spend limits.

charts.modelsLead: What your day would cost with each model alone, without an advisor or subagents. The difference is price per token: Opus 5.5 costs twice Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 five times, and Haiku 5.5 a fraction.
charts.strategiesLead: Each model doing what it does best: Sonnet builds, Haiku explores, Opus reviews.
charts.trioNote: The trick going around social media is `claude --advisor opus --subagents haiku`. The `--advisor` flag exists, but `--subagents` isn't in the documentation. The documented way to run subagents on Haiku is the environment variable:
charts.trioWhy: The advisor reads the whole conversation on every call, uncached, so it adds cost. What it buys is quality on hard decisions without paying for Opus all the time.
charts.breakdownLead: Claude Code resends the whole conversation with every request. That's why almost all tokens are cache reads: dirt cheap per token, but there are millions. In dollars, cache writes and output weigh more: few tokens, but expensive. Short sessions and /clear shrink both.

start.d: Day 1: install, give it context, ask well.

habits.d: Week 1: plan, verify, pick a model.

extend.d: Month 1: skills, MCP, hooks, subagents and plugins.

route.title: Your trail
route.lead: Each step is a short lesson with a terminal to practice and a test. They unlock in order: pass the test to open the next one.

install.d: Install Claude Code, open a terminal in your project and type claude. Sign in with your Pro or Max plan, or with an API key.

init.d: /init reads your project and writes a CLAUDE.md with commands, conventions and structure. Claude reads it at the start of every session.

prompting.d: Say which file, which scenario and how it knows it's done. Vague requests make it scan the whole project and spend more.
prompting.p: Users can't log in after their session expires. Check src/auth, especially the token refresh. Write a failing test, fix it and run the tests.

modes.d: Shift+Tab cycles between Manual (asks for everything), accept edits, plan mode and auto. In auto, a classifier checks each action in the background.

mentions.d: @ mentions a file so Claude reads it. ! runs a command in your shell and adds the output to the conversation.

interrupt.d: Esc stops Claude without losing work done. Esc twice or /rewind takes the conversation and code back to an earlier point.

context.d: /clear starts fresh, /compact summarizes what came before and /context shows what takes up space. Small context = better and cheaper answers.

usage.d: /usage shows what the session spent, how much of your plan is left and which skills, MCP servers or subagents use the most.

planmode.d: The recommended flow: plan mode to read and propose, you approve the plan, Claude implements and then commits. If you could describe the diff in one sentence, skip the plan.

verify.t: Give it a way to verify
verify.d: The single biggest quality boost: tests, a screenshot to compare against, or expected output. If it can check its own work, it fixes its own mistakes.
verify.p: Write a validateEmail function. Cases: user@example.com is valid, invalid is not, user@.com is not. Run the tests after implementing.

models.d: /model switches models and /effort sets how much it reasons. Put ultrathink in a prompt for deeper reasoning on that turn only.

sessions.d: claude --continue resumes the last session and /resume picks one. /rename names it and /branch tries another direction without losing the current one.

btw.d: /btw asks a quick question about the session without adding it to the conversation or cluttering the context.

images.d: Paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V: a design to build, an on-screen error or a chart. Claude sees it and compares it with the result.

review.d: /diff shows the changes, /code-review looks for bugs in your diff and /security-review looks for vulnerabilities.

automode.d: Claude works without asking permission at every step, with safety checks in the background. For long tasks.

claudemd.d: Under 200 lines: commands it couldn't guess, rules specific to the project and known gotchas. Anything not always needed goes in a skill.

skills.d: A SKILL.md with instructions or a workflow (deploy, release, review). Only the description takes up context until it's used. Invoke it with /name.

mcp.d: Connects Claude to external services: GitHub, Notion, Slack, databases, Figma. Tools load on demand. If a CLI exists (gh, aws), it usually costs less.

hooks.d: Scripts that run on their own at events: format after every edit or block dangerous commands. They use no context unless they return something. They're rules that always hold, not requests.

subagents.d: Claude delegates a task to an agent with its own context (Explore, Plan or your own) and gets back only the summary. Your conversation stays clean.

plugins.d: Packages that bundle skills, hooks, subagents and MCP together. Install them from /plugin, including Anthropic's official marketplaces.

codeintel.d: Language server plugins (TypeScript, Python…). Claude jumps to definitions and sees type errors as it edits, instead of reading whole files.

mods.d: Change Claude Code's interface and behavior: panes, your own commands and rules on tool calls. Ask Claude to write one for you.

styles.d: Change the tone and format of every response: more concise, more explanatory, or a role other than software engineer.

statusline.d: A bar with whatever you always want to see: model, context %, cost, git branch.

advisor.d: Claude consults a stronger model before committing to an approach, when an error keeps recurring, or before calling something done. Enable it with --advisor, /advisor or advisorModel.

subagentModel.t: Sonnet builds, Haiku explores, Opus reviews
subagentModel.d: Session on Sonnet, subagents on Haiku and Opus as the advisor: each model on its own job. Note: --subagents isn't a documented flag; use the CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL variable.

opusplan.d: Uses Opus while you're in plan mode and switches to Sonnet to implement. Think expensive, execute cheap.

loop.d: Repeats a prompt on an interval while the session stays open: watch a deploy, check CI. Each run resends the context, so mind the interval.

routines.d: Scheduled tasks that run in the cloud even when your computer is off: review PRs every morning, audit dependencies.

background.d: /background lets the session keep going on its own, /fork copies it and /subtask launches a subagent with the whole conversation. claude agents shows them all.

worktrees.d: Several sessions in parallel on the same repo without stepping on each other: each one in its own git worktree.

goal.d: Give it a completion condition and Claude keeps working, turn after turn, until it's met.

workflows.d: For jobs that outgrow a couple of subagents: Claude writes a script that splits the task across many agents and cross-checks the results.

teams.d: Several Claude instances with shared tasks and messaging. Experimental: uses about 7 times more tokens with teammates in plan mode.

headless.t: Headless mode and the Agent SDK
headless.d: claude -p runs without the interface, for scripts and CI. The Agent SDK (Python and TypeScript) lets you build your own agents on Claude Code's engine.

github.d: Mention @claude in an issue or PR and it answers, reviews or opens a PR from Actions.

chrome.d: Claude opens your app in the browser, clicks around, reads the console and checks that the change really works.

insights.d: A report on how you work: which projects, where things get stuck and which features you should try.

runverify.d: Claude launches your app and checks the change really works, not just that tests pass. /run-skill-generator teaches it how to start your project.

simplify.d: Before committing, four agents review your change for duplicated code, needless complexity and slowness, and apply the fixes.

skilldoctor.d: Shows how many tokens each skill costs and how often you use it. Turn off the extras: every description takes up context on every message.

fewerprompts.d: Looks at your sessions and allows the safe commands you use most, so it stops asking permission for every ls or git status.

debug.d: When something doesn't work (a hook that doesn't run, an MCP server that won't connect), /debug turns on the log and reads it for you. /doctor checks the whole install and proposes fixes.

deepresearch.d: A bundled workflow that searches the web in parallel, cross-checks sources and hands you a cited report.

ultrareview.d: Deep multi-agent review in the cloud before merging. /autofix-pr watches your PR and pushes fixes when CI fails.

remote.t: From your phone or another computer
remote.d: /remote-control opens the session on claude.ai or the mobile app, /teleport pulls a cloud session into your terminal and /desktop moves it to the desktop app.

anatomy.title: Anatomy of a good prompt
goodParts: Users can't log in after their session expires.
Check src/auth, especially the token refresh.
Write a test that reproduces the error, fix it and run the tests.
Find the root cause, don't patch the symptom.
anatomy.why: The first one forces Claude to guess and read half the project. The second tells it what's happening, where to look, how to check it's done and what to avoid.

save: /clear whenever you switch tasks. A short message in a long session rereads the whole history.
Sonnet for everyday work; Opus or Fable only for hard decisions. Better yet: Sonnet with Opus as the advisor.
Run subagents on Haiku with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku.
Lower the effort (/effort low) for mechanical tasks.
If a CLI exists (gh, aws), it's lighter than an MCP server. Turn off MCP servers you don't use with /mcp.
Keep CLAUDE.md short; specifics go in skills.
After more than an hour idle the cache expires and the first message reprocesses everything. Better to /clear than to resume something huge.
tips.maxTitle: Get the most out of it
max: Always give it a way to verify: tests, screenshots, expected output.
Plan mode when you're unsure of the approach or touching many files.
An Opus advisor on long tasks: refactors, recurring bugs.
One session writes and another reviews: the reviewer isn't biased by its own code.
Worktrees and background agents to work in parallel.
Hooks for what must always happen; skills for what needs judgment.
Run /insights now and then to see where you lose time.

guide.title: Claude Code cheat sheet
guide.lead: The commands, shortcuts and modes most worth knowing. All checked against the official documentation.
guide.empty: No command matches “{q}”. Try another word.
guide.skillsLead: They ship with Claude Code: nothing to install. Invoke them with /name, and Claude also uses them on its own when they help.
guide.communityLead: The most used ones, with GitHub stars as of October 18, 2026. They're not from Anthropic: review each one before installing.
guide.askillsLead: The official anthropics/skills repo: Office documents and PDF, design, generative art, web testing and more. Installed as two bundles.
guide.knowledgeLead: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins has 123 plugins for work beyond code. These are Anthropic's own, one per area.

commands.btw: Side question, not added to the conversation.
commands.diff: Reviews the changes in your working tree.
commands.code-review: Looks for bugs in your diff, a PR or a branch. --fix applies them.
commands.security-review: Looks for vulnerabilities in your branch's changes.

commands.goal: Claude works until a condition is met.

commands.batch: Large changes in parallel: splits into 5 to 30 units.

commands.add-dir: Adds another working directory to the session.
commands.cd: Moves the session to another directory without losing the conversation.
commands.terminal-setup: Installs Shift+Enter for new lines in VS Code, Cursor, Alacritty or Zed.
commands.voice: Voice dictation: hold or tap to record.
commands.usage-credits: Usage credits to keep working when you hit your plan's limit.
commands.rate-limit-options: Options when you hit a limit: wait and continue automatically, credits, or upgrade.
commands.release-notes: Changelog by version, without adding it to the conversation.
commands.artifacts: Lists your artifacts to attach them to the session, open them or copy the link.
commands.auto-mode-setup: Drafts your auto mode setup from your project and recent sessions.
commands.config: Opens settings, or sets a value directly: /config theme=dark.
commands.copy: Copies the last response, or a code block, to the clipboard.
commands.branch: Branches the conversation to try another direction without losing the current one.
commands.theme: Changes the color theme, including colorblind-friendly themes.
commands.tui: Changes the terminal renderer; fullscreen avoids flicker.
commands.reload-skills: Rescans for new or edited skills without restarting.
commands.list-agents: Lists the subagents, teammates and sessions Claude can message.
commands.artifact-capabilities: What a published artifact can do: use your connectors, offer downloads and more.
commands.artifact-diagramming: Guidance for Claude to draw SVG diagrams that read well in light and dark mode.
commands.claude-api: Claude API and Managed Agents reference: migrate models, audit prompts, optimize cost.
commands.claude-in-chrome: Claude does a task in your browser: test a page, fill a form, read the console.
commands.dataviz: Chart and dashboard guidance: picks the form, validates the palette for colorblindness and contrast.
commands.debug: Turns on debug logging and reads it to diagnose session problems.
commands.deep-research: Workflow: searches the web in parallel, cross-checks sources and writes a cited report.
commands.design: Mockups of screens, flows or landing pages as artboards on a Claude Design canvas.

commands.run: Launches and drives your app to see the change working, not just green tests.
commands.run-skill-generator: Teaches /run and /verify how to build and launch your app, with a project skill.

commands.slides: Builds a presentation as a Claude Slides artifact from your brief.

commands.verify: Confirms a change does what it should: builds, runs and observes the app.
commands.workflow-authoring: Reference for writing dynamic workflow scripts.

shortcuts.cycleModes: Cycles permission modes (Manual, accept edits, plan, auto).
shortcuts.interrupt: Stops Claude without losing work done.
shortcuts.rewind: With empty input, opens the rewind menu.
shortcuts.shell: At the start: runs a shell command.
shortcuts.editor: Edits the prompt (or the plan) in your editor.
shortcuts.pasteImage: Pastes an image from the clipboard.
shortcuts.background: Sends commands and agents to the background.
shortcuts.todo: Shows or hides Claude's task list.
shortcuts.stash: Stashes a half-written prompt and restores it.

shortcuts.fastToggle: Turns fast mode on or off.
shortcuts.help: With empty input, shows all shortcuts.

modes.default: Manual: only reads without asking. For sensitive work or unfamiliar code.
modes.acceptEdits: Edits files and runs basic file commands without asking.
modes.plan: Reads and proposes a plan; doesn't edit until you approve it.
modes.auto: Does everything, with safety checks in the background. For long tasks.
modes.dontAsk: Only pre-approved actions; everything else is denied. For CI and scripts.
modes.bypassPermissions: Everything without asking. Only in isolated containers or VMs.

modGuide.lead: A mod is a plugin with JavaScript or TypeScript code that runs inside Claude Code. Unlike hooks, skills and MCP, it can draw in the interface and step into every event.
can: Draw panes beside the conversation or a band above the prompt, with tabs, buttons and text fields.
Change what Claude Code already draws: a tool call's row, the spinner, the question dialog.
Hold or change a tool call: ask you something first, answer it without running the tool, or send a request to another model.
Add a /command that runs your function instantly, without spending a Claude turn.
Share data between events: for example, count tool calls and show the number next to the spinner.

samples.token-weather: A weather forecast for your context window above the prompt.
samples.blast-radius: Holds risky commands (rm -rf, force push), shows what they'd change and lets you proceed or cancel.
samples.replay-theater: Adds /replay to step through the last turn's file edits.

modGuide.create: Describe what you want to Claude: it loads the /plugin-authoring skill and writes the mod for you. Then reload with /reload-plugins.
modGuide.builtin: You already use mods: /diff is a built-in one. In /plugin, Installed tab, they're listed under Built-in.
modGuide.safety: A mod runs with your permissions and no sandbox: it reads and writes files, sees your prompts and can approve tools without asking. Install only from authors you know, and check what it does before installing:

pluginGuide.lead: A plugin bundles skills, hooks, subagents, MCP servers and mods into something you install with one command. The official marketplace comes pre-added and has {total} plugins: {anthropic} from Anthropic and the rest from companies like GitHub, Figma or Vercel.
pluginGuide.install: Browse with /plugin (Discover tab) or at claude.com/marketplace/plugins. To install one:
pluginGuide.lsp: One plugin per language: Claude jumps to definitions and sees type errors as it edits.
pluginGuide.community: There's also a community marketplace: /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-community. Anthropic doesn't review third-party marketplaces, so read the plugin security page before adding one.
pluginGuide.snapshot: Catalog checked on October 18, 2026. It changes often.

recs.title: Recommended for your role
recs.lead: Pick your role and we'll show which skills, plugins and repos are worth adding, with the command to install them.
recs.saversLead: Useful for any role. Each project publishes its own savings figures: measure with /usage before and after.

community.caveman: Makes Claude answer short and to the point. The project claims an average 65% cut in output tokens.
community.rtk: Rust proxy that compresses terminal command output before it enters the context. Claims 60% to 90% savings.
community.headroom: Compresses tool output, logs and files before they reach the model.
community.context-mode: Sandboxes tool output and keeps session memory so the context doesn't fill up.
community.claude-mem: Persistent memory across sessions: records what the agent does, compresses it and brings it back when needed.

terms.title: Terms and conditions
body: Procode is a free guide to learning Claude Code. By using the site you accept these terms.
The content is educational. Usage and cost figures are estimates based on public prices and may not match your actual bill; always check the official documentation before choosing a plan.

If you sign in with GitHub or Google, we store only your account name, your answers and your progress, so you can continue on another device. Without an account, progress lives in the tab and is cleared when you close it. We do not sell or share your data.
Commands and examples are provided as is. Review what you run on your machine; we are not liable for damage resulting from their use.
The design, texts and the Tilde mascot belong to their author. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic.
We may update these terms; the date above shows the latest version. For questions or complaints, use the Help form at the bottom of the page.
terms.mail: Email reminders: only if you turn them on, we use your account email to let you know when 2 days pass without a visit, once per absence. Turn them off anytime from your achievements.
